title: Connecting finite-size scaling and renormalization-group flows in Anderson localization on random graphs
authors: Ignacio García-Mata, Weitao Chen, John Martin, Bertrand Georgeot, Gabriel Lemarié
abstract: We investigate the relation between two complementary descriptions of the Anderson transition on small-world random graphs: finite-size scaling of eigenfunction moments and renormalization-group (RG) flows of multifractal dimensions $D_q$. The RG flows recover the qualitative structure previously reported for the information dimension $D_1$, while their extension to other $D_q$ with smaller moment orders $q<1/2$ confirms the strongly multifractal nature of the localized phase characterized by a clear separation between multifractal and localized behaviors at strong disorder. On the other hand, we show that we can construct another beta function characterizing the flow of eigenfunction moments, whose collapse onto a single function across different disorder strengths provides a clear confirmation of single-parameter scaling property. These results indicate that the family of RG trajectories observed for the information dimension $D_1$ need not imply two-parameter scaling and Kosterlitz-Thouless like critical behavior. To characterize these properties, one should consider different observables, such as large $q>1/2$ and small $q<1/2$ eigenfunction moments, which are associated with distinct critical behaviors, in particular different critical exponents.
summary: This paper compares finite-size scaling and renormalization-group approaches to characterize the Anderson transition on random graphs. It finds that while different observables yield different scaling behaviors, the system's critical properties can be consistently described by a single-parameter scaling function derived from normalized eigenfunction moments. This clarifies the underlying scaling structure, suggesting that the apparent complexity of the RG flow might stem from the choice of observable rather than intrinsic multi-parameter physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the relationship between two complementary theoretical descriptions—finite-size scaling (FSS) of eigenfunction moments and renormalization-group (RG) flows of multifractal dimensions ($D_q$)—for the Anderson transition on random graphs.
main_result: The analysis shows that while the RG flow for $D_1$ might suggest a two-parameter scaling, the structure is highly dependent on the moment order $q$. A single-parameter scaling can be confirmed by constructing a $ eta$ function for normalized moments that collapses across different disorder strengths.
method: The authors employ both FSS techniques using eigenfunction moments and RG flow analysis using multifractal dimensions ($D_q$). They compare the scaling behavior derived from these two approaches.
model_or_system: The system is Anderson localization on small-world random graphs (SWRGs). The Hamiltonian includes random site energies ($\epsilon_i$) and hopping terms, including nearest-neighbor and long-range random hoppings.
key_observables: Eigenfunction moments ($P_q$), generalized multifractal dimensions ($D_q$), and the running $ eta$ functions ($ eta_q$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), graph size ($N$), and the moment order ($q$). The critical point is associated with $q=1/2$.
main_assumptions: The central point is distinguishing between a true two-parameter scaling structure (suggested by comparing different observables) and an apparent two-dimensional flow from a single observable due to non-trivial size dependence.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the collapse of normalized moments ($F_q$) for different $q$ values, showing how different scaling regimes (volumetric vs. linear) govern the flow on either side of the transition.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the scaling predictions from FSS (using moment collapse) against those from RG (using $D_q$ flow). It develops the mathematical framework to reconcile the scale conversions between the two methods, concluding that the physical flow retains a single-parameter structure even if the initial observables suggest otherwise.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical comparison between two advanced scaling theories (FSS and RG) applied to a fundamental quantum problem (Anderson localization), offering insights into the nature of critical exponents and scaling dimensionality in disordered quantum systems.
